title: Take-up Rate by Malay/Muslims of Existing National Financial and Estate Planning Programmes
what_it_is: Take-up Rate by Malay/Muslims of Existing National Financial and Estate Planning Programmes

sections.label: Program Bijak Belanja participants
sections.summary: Over two and a half years, more than 600 participants have benefited from MENDAKI SENSE's Program Bijak Belanja.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Over the last two and a half years, more than 600 participants have benefited from MENDAKI SENSE's Program Bijak Belanja.

sections.label: MUIS and MoneySENSE financial planning
sections.summary: MUIS is discussing with MoneySENSE to incorporate financial planning components into this programme, expected to be implemented next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS) is in discussion with MoneySENSE to incorporate financial planning components into this programme, which is expected to be implemented next year.

sections.label: Hibah SNTC Fatwa trusts
sections.summary: The Hibah Special Needs Trust Company Fatwa permits trusts for disabled dependents to ensure their future well-being when no caregiver survives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For example, the Hibah Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) Fatwa permits trusts to be made for disabled dependents to ensure their future well-being when there is no longer a surviving caregiver.

sections.label: Wakaf Ilmu charitable endowment
sections.summary: In 2012, MUIS set up the Wakaf Ilmu, a voluntary charitable endowment for Muslims to do planned giving.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In 2012, MUIS also set up the "Wakaf Ilmu", a voluntary charitable endowment for Muslims to come forward to do planned giving.

sections.label: EIP limits and appeals
sections.summary: EIP numbers rose from 2017 to 2019, with 59% from Indian and other communities, and the question asks whether the 2020 EIP review was undertaken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This has been on the up, from 2017 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand the numbers were around 1,850 for the three years: 25% from the Malay community, 16% from the Chinese community and 59% from the Indian and other communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My question is: for the EIP limit for the Indian and other communities, which was at 59%, when the EIP limit overall was actually reviewed in 2010, the EIP limit for that category was 10% and 13% at the neighbourhood and block level, and that was increased to 12% and 15% respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My question is: in view of the large number of EIP appeals continuing to come from this community and a suggestion made in 2010 by the then-Minister for National Development that there would be a review around 2020, has this review been undertaken and what are the new EIP limits, if any?

sections.label: HDB flexibility on EIP criteria
sections.summary: The question asks whether HDB would consider a similar approach for all flats and greater neighbourhood flexibility, or remove precinct and block quotas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would HDB consider a similar approach for all flats and also exercise greater flexibility at the neighbourhood level as a means of loosening the EIP criteria as a compromise, or even remove precinct and block quotas in favour of a larger area of coverage?

sections.label: EIP limits neighbourhood numbers
sections.summary: In 1989, 28% of neighbourhoods reached one or more EIP limits; in June 2021, 14% of 173 neighbourhoods breached one or more ethnic limits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In 1989, when we introduced the EIP, 28% of neighbourhoods had reached one or more EIP limits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In June this year, out of 173 neighbourhoods – because we have been building our towns and increasing the number of neighbourhoods – 14% have breached one or more ethnic limits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In 1989, 35 neighbourhoods out of 125 and in June 2021, 24 out of 173.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, more neighbourhoods as a whole in Singapore but the number of neighbourhoods hitting one or more EIP limits has come down, not just in proportionate terms but in absolute numbers.

sections.label: Waiving EIP limits individually
sections.summary: The speaker says individual cases should determine whether to waive the limit, rather than raising EIP limits for all races, as the Chinese limit is already 87%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And I hope the Member agrees with me.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Therefore, we look at individual cases in order to determine whether we should waive the limit as opposed to an inexorable increase in EIP limits for all races across the board, which for some cases would bring it close to 100% because for Chinese, the EIP limit is already 87%.

sections.label: Diversity at home and neighbourhoods
sections.summary: The speaker asks why diversity concerns in workplace, National Service, schools and social mixing should not also apply at home and in neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: If you are concerned about diversity in the workplace, in National Service, in national schools and even social mixing – I recall there was an Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) discussion about different socio-economic classes and the concern about whether they mix – then, why not at home and in our neighbourhoods where we spend a vast amount of time?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: It would help to advance our common understanding.

sections.label: Economic loss to minority sellers
sections.summary: The passage states the WP position since 2006 concerns economic loss to minorities who lower their flats' market price, citing one seller's $100,000 loss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Number four, as it is well known – this is really the heartbeat of why WP has taken the position it has since 2006.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: It was, I think, referred to as a "time bomb" by PAP even then – and that is the economic loss to minorities who have to lower the market price of their flats in the name of that policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: That is particularly painful because we hear that from many people who are in that position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I believe the Chairperson of WP in the opening of the Parliament for this session, referred to one individual who had to sell the flat at a loss of $100,000.

sections.label: Loosening EIP quota or area
sections.summary: The passage suggests loosening the EIP quota with HDB buying back affected flats at valuation, or using a larger geographical area instead of precinct and block quotas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In its current form, as I suggested, the EIP quota should either be further loosened to ameliorate the prospects of further economic loss for sellers with HDB committed to buying back the affected flat at the valuation price, or a larger geographical area representing the anchor for the EIP rather than the precinct and block quotas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Would the MND be prepared to release that information?

sections.label: EIP origins from 1960s lessons
sections.summary: The passage states the EIP was not pre-emptive in 1989 but was put in place because of lessons learnt from the 1960s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It is not a pre-emptive policy in 1989.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It was a policy that was put in place because of the lessons learnt from the 1960s, paid for with blood, sweat and tears.

sections.label: HDB EIP waiver for family
sections.summary: HDB waived the EIP in August 2019 to let a family sell, but the family declined and asked HDB to acquire the flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We were not in a position to verify what the offers were for that flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But in that case, HDB assessed the case holistically and agreed in August 2019 to waive the EIP for a period of time to allow the family to sell.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Waived off EIP, looking at the circumstances of the family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But the family decided not to take this offer up for other reasons and requested HDB to acquire the flat.

sections.label: EIP appeals and multi-racial support
sections.summary: Appeals are scrutinised to help affected sellers, and EIP is reviewed to keep support for multi-racial measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And we address that through appeals, we look at these and scrutinise very carefully to help the affected seller.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And as we said, we continue to look at how we can smoothen the rough edges of EIP and ensure that a new generation of Singaporeans who have not lived through the tumultuous early days of Singapore history continue to support measures, may not be popular measures, but necessary bulwarks to ensure that our multi-racial character is in substance and not in form.

sections.label: Ethnic concentration and multi-racialism
sections.summary: It asks whether accepting ethnic concentration is fine because multi-racialism exists in National Service, schools and workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Or is it the case that you accept that given even current trends, there will be a lot of concentration, but that it is perfectly okay, there is no impact to our multi-racial character because we have multi-racialism in National Service, in our national schools and our workplaces?

sections.label: Ethnic quotas beyond housing
sections.summary: It asks whether ethnic quotas should move to schools, workplaces, pre-schools, markets, hawker centres and shops, and mentions data will be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Does he then say, we move the EIP away from housing and put ethnic quotas in schools, in workplaces, in pre-schools, in markets, in hawker centres, in neighbourhood shops?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Or you think it is fine that the schools and pre-schools, they are all ethnically focused because its proximity and it is fine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We are sufficiently multicultural – a point you have made since 2006, that Singapore has reached such a high level of multiculturalism that we no longer need to concern ourselves with mixing people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As for the last point about the data, we will look at what data we can provide, the granularity, it changes from month to month.

sections.label: HDB rental block limits review
sections.summary: It asks what scheme changes HDB discussed for the review due 10 years after 2010, beyond case-by-case and rental block limit flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Beyond these cases where HDB looks at it on a case-by-case basis, we have a regime, the rental housing regime, where HDB is prepared to administratively lift block limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: There is flexibility beyond looking at individual cases and moving the boundaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, the question I like to ask is for the review that was supposed to take place 10 years after 2010, according to Minister Mah Bow Tan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: What sort of scheme changes have HDB discussed internally, beyond just looking at cases on a case-by-case basis?

sections.label: Workers' Party manifesto abolish
sections.summary: The Workers' Party, in its manifesto, has said, abolish it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Workers' Party, in its manifesto, has said, abolish it.

sections.label: Workers' Party EIP position change
sections.summary: The Workers' Party called for immediate abolition of EIP from 2006, but in 2021 says EIP is still needed while working towards a race-blind society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In 2006 and all the way till last year, the Workers' Party position was that we have already reached a level of multiculturalism and, therefore, unequivocally, called for since 2006, election after election, for the immediate abolition of EIP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But the Workers' Party's position today, in 2021, is that we still need the EIP, we work towards a race-blind society and we endeavour to reach there and, at some point, hopefully, we may not need EIP.

sections.label: MOE reviews CCE curriculum
sections.summary: The Ministry of Education regularly reviews the CCE curriculum to equip students with necessary skills and keep up with a complex environment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) regularly reviews the CCE curriculum to ensure that our students are equipped with the necessary skills and keep up with the increasingly complex and dynamic environment.

sections.label: New CCE 2021 curriculum
sections.summary: The new CCE 2021 curriculum builds on the previous one and strengthens focus on character, values, competencies and citizenship dispositions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The new CCE 2021 curriculum builds on the foundation that have been laid by the previous CCE curriculum and further strengthens the focus on guiding students to build character, learn values, social and emotional competencies, and develop citizenship dispositions within and beyond the classrooms.

sections.label: Project DIAN@M3 outreach focus
sections.summary: Project DIAN@M3 will focus on outreach to families in rental flats and build on M3's partnerships with Government agencies and Malay/Muslim organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I will take it as a whole and try to answer the questions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: So, as I have shared earlier, for now, Project DIAN@M3 will focus on outreach to families staying in rental flats and build upon the partnerships which M3 has earlier on developed with Government agencies and Malay/Muslim organisations.

sections.label: Project DIAN@M3 launch and goals
sections.summary: Project DIAN@M3 launches in the fourth quarter starting with Bedok, Geylang Serai and Jalan Besar, aiming to strengthen families and move them towards home ownership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In doing so, we hope to also cultivate values, such as independence and resilience, in these families as they journey towards home ownership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will launch Project DIAN@M3 in the fourth quarter of this year, where we will start with three M3@Towns, namely Bedok, Geylang Serai and Jalan Besar.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As we journey through this process, we hope that we will be able to strengthen families, provide opportunities for the Malay/Muslim families, especially those in rental flats, and, at the same time, give them and work with the Government agencies and our partners for them to move towards home ownership in the years to come.

sections.label: Muslims dying intestate
sections.summary: Today, there are still many Muslims in Singapore who passed away intestate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, today, there are still many Muslims in Singapore who passed away intestate.

sections.label: Programme drew 600 people
sections.summary: The programme attracted a full house of about 600 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The programme attracted a full house; a total of about 600 people came.

sections.label: Replicating programmes across M3 towns
sections.summary: The speaker says the programmes discussed have been successful and wants to replicate them in as many M3 towns as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I think these programmes that I have talked about have been successful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We want to replicate it to as many towns as possible in M3.

sections.label: Safe feedback and racism reports
sections.summary: It ensures feedback is given in a safe, confidential environment, and racism incidents in schools are not tolerated and reports are thoroughly investigated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: More importantly, it is to ensure that they are able to provide the feedback in a safe environment and that they feel assured that their feedback will be taken in strict confidence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: I want to assure again that any incidents of racism are not tolerated in any of the schools and any report that we receive will be thoroughly investigated.

sections.label: Provision not invoked
sections.summary: Members may know the provision has not been used and has not had to be invoked.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: What is also useful about it is that Members may know that it has not been used, we have not had to invoke it.

sections.label: Malay educational progress statistics
sections.summary: Malay P1 cohort post-secondary participation doubled in 25 years, university graduates doubled from 5.5% in 2010 to 10.8% in 2020, and Malay students scored above OECD average in PISA 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The relevant Ministries will give more full answer, I am sure, in due course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But if you take some of the points raised in these PQs, we are able to say that the percentage of Malay P1 cohort going onto post-Secondary education has doubled in the last 25 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The number of Malay university graduates has doubled from 5.5% in 2010 to 10.8% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If we take the average Malay student, they were found in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) in 2018 to have scored higher, above the OECD average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And Malay students also outperformed international students in this same PISA assessment on 21st century competencies.

sections.label: Post-1990 immigration and CMIO
sections.summary: Immigration after 1990 changed Singapore society, raising the question of whether CMIO alone still applies or something more complicated is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: More than that, I think, immigration after 1990 has changed the complexion of Singapore society in that, are we just looking at CMIO now or is there something a little bit more complicated in Singapore that we need to look into?

sections.label: Census and CMIO model
sections.summary: Census 2010 broke down the Indian community into minority languages like Urdu and Gujarathi, while Census 2020 takes a narrower approach with some categories falling away.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In the census, if you look at Census 2010 for the Indian community, for example, it was broken down into the minority languages: Urdu, Gujarathi.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But Census 2020 takes a much more narrow approach; some categories have fallen away.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I do believe that there is a fundamental shift in Singapore society and it will be useful to know if the CMIO model needs to evolve.

sections.label: HDB policies and EIP
sections.summary: The speaker says HDB policies and EIP are more likely to achieve multi-racial integrated communities than what the WP proposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Speaker, Sir, I think there is a lesson to be learnt here between philosophy and methods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We want Singaporeans to live together in multi-racial communities, not in segregated communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But we have the same philosophy that we want a multi-racial society Singapore, integrated housing, well-integrated communities and schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We are more likely to get there with the HDB policies that we have today, with EIP, rather than what the WP is proposing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In fact, their manifesto says abolish it now; although the Leader of the Opposition seems to have shifted away from that because he realises that that is untenable.
